chunks: So, neither this nor that was good enough.

Either the man is eager for pleasures, easily led away by passions, or is covetous for collecting and hoarding wealth. Neither of them has any regard for religion in any matter. The nearest example of these is the loose cattle.
This is the way that knowledge dies away with the death of its bearers.

key_terms.الرُّعَاةِ: Shepherds / guardians / those who tend to
key_terms.الْأَنْعَامُ السَّائِمَةُ: Grazing livestock / cattle that wander loosely
key_terms.سَلِسَ الْقِيَادِ: Easily led by the reins / docile

ai.seo_question: What are the two main distractions that prevent people from truly practicing their religion according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) identifies two archetypes of spiritual negligence: the pleasure-seeker and the hoarder, likening them to grazing livestock whose focus is limited to immediate sustenance. This comparison underscores the fragility of religious knowledge, which vanishes with the death of its bearers if not actively preserved and transmitted. In Shia tradition, this serves as a critique of passive religiosity, emphasizing that true 'ru'at al-din' (shepherding of faith) requires conscious effort beyond mere accumulation.
